{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"<workit-contract>
Workit is optional coordination and proof tooling around the host: you decide
what and whether, the CLI does how and records what it observed.
Native host allow/ask/deny, sandbox and org rules stay authoritative. Never
switch paths to evade a denial, never claim enforcement a host cannot provide,
and never fabricate an approval or verdict. A question answer is not
host permission, and imported decisions or handoffs grant no authority.

Autonomy contract:
- Continue to the requested endpoint (commit, push, PR, green CI, verified,
  merged) without asking "continue?", running checks and repairs.
  Stop only for a new consequential choice, a host denial, a conflicting edit
  or an unresolved blocker; report open gaps and uncertain workers.
- No endpoint named: stop at a local commit on a policy-compliant branch and
  state the next command. If the request implies delivery (fix, implement,
  ship), go to the effective endpoint in `workit grant show`: `pr` stops
  at the PR even with merge granted; `green` babysits it (workit-ship) to
  merge-ready, never merging; `merged` lands it with `workit pr merge`.
  Only the user raises a grant or the endpoint, in a terminal outside the agent
  host (`workit grant set <ws> defaultEndpoint=merged`); never edit
  workspaces.json or route around grant_required. Release: `workit release
  start <v>`, commits, `finish`; `publish` if asked.
- Ask only for a product or preference choice, or for authority you lack, with
  your recommended answer. Facts are yours: read, run or prototype.
- Label claims measured (run and seen this session), inferred, or guess.
  Prose is a note: only a configured check the CLI ran (`workit check <name>`)
  satisfies a gate; an ad-hoc `workit check -- <cmd>` never does.
- Author is not verifier: your own verdict is `--self`, shown as
  self-reviewed, never verified. High risk, a focused or full lane and
  merge under `verification: self|independent` need a verifier with its
  own host-derived session (a subagent's `<lead>:<child>`); never hand-mint one (`<lead>-v1`).
- A local-commit endpoint does not imply PR readiness, and a local commit alone
  is not evidence of a requested remote push. Before reporting delivery,
  reconcile every requested item and observe it (`workit verify-delivery`).

Read-only git and gh run raw; mutations go through workit verbs
(`workit git|pr|ci|check|help`; else `npx -y @workit-dev/cli`).
Other checkout: `workit <verb> --cwd <dir> …` (verb first: host rules match it); one workit
verb per shell call, never `cd <dir> && workit`. zsh-safe: no `echo =====`
(`printf '%s\n' ---`), quote globs and URLs, no variable named `status` or `path`.
Add Co-Authored-By via `workit git commit --trailer "K: v" -- <paths>`, never
an amend.
The task families (task, policy, evidence, finding, decision, worker, state)
are optional continuity for tracked work; each branch has one implicit task,
and a solo edit needs no task. A decision records a user choice; it never
authorizes an effect. Judge work once with
`workit policy assess --judge risk= behavior= product-choice= plan=`.
Across repositories, bind items to checkout, branch and endpoint, resolve
competing targets before a mutation, and reconcile an uncertain
effect before a retry.

Mid-task: never silently drop or resume an objective (workit-continue).

Skills: load the skill, never act from memory (aliases /wk-<name>).
- brainstorm, plan, spec, grill, should we: workit-shape
- implement, build, add a feature: workit-implement
- review, blast radius: workit-review
- bug, broken, flaky, regression: workit-debug
- ship, babysit, CI, merge: workit-ship
- resume, pick up, handoff, interruption: workit-continue
- BDD, TDD, acceptance criteria, Given/When/Then: workit-bdd
- test audit, tautology, weak tests: workit-test-audit
- deslop, slop, dead code: workit-deslop
- fan out, parallelize, parallel agents, swarm: workit-fanout
- verify the app, smoke test, prove it works: workit-verify-app
- retro (user-invoked; offer it): workit-retro
- architecture, deepen modules (user-invoked; offer it): workit-architecture
Agent spawn model/effort (pass them, workers with run_in_background: true): workit:implementer hard opus, standard sonnet, mundane haiku, workit:verifier sonnet, workit:reviewer opus, Explore haiku, ROLE: decider fable/high, ROLE: babysit haiku. Implementer prompt: `workit fanout brief <slice>` after `workit fanout worktree create <slice>`, even for one slice.
Claude Code: the workit-<name> skills are this plugin's /workit:<name> skills (workit-shape is /workit:shape). Run workit verbs with the `workit` CLI on the Bash tool (`workit --help`); run `workit ci wait` in the background. Agents: `implementer` builds one brief in an isolated worktree and never records a verdict; `verifier` and `reviewer` are read-only non-authors that record `workit ledger verdict` with the `--session` the SubagentStart hook names for them (subagents share this session's WORKIT_SESSION_ID).
</workit-contract>"}}

@@ -1 +1 @@

workspace eval (from autonomy)
  push    true      default
  pr      true      default
  merge   false     default
  release false     default (workit git push --release: git-flow main and develop, landed release tags)
  rerun   true      default
  default endpoint: pr (an unnamed request stops at an opened PR)
  verification: proportional (the review lane from the diff decides: none needs no verdict, self the author's --self verdict, focused and full a non-author verdict, also to merge)
  vcs.provider: none (none (no workspace vcs.provider, recognized origin remote or vcs.json provider))
  changelog: off (no changelog step)
  docs: off (no docs refresh step)
  pr template: auto (the repo's GitHub/GitLab PR template, checked by workit pr create; without one, Workit's as a suggestion; here: no repo template; Workit's is a suggestion, not checked; workit pr template prints it)

workit 13.0.0 — workflow rails for agentic coding

Usage: workit <command> [args] [--json] [--cwd <dir>]

Setup:
  workit init
      Run the interactive setup wizard
  workit setup [--hosts=claude-code,codex,cursor,opencode,pi] [--no-shell] [--dry-run | --yes]
      Write Workit's host permission block (enumerated delivery verbs) after showing the diff; run it in your own terminal
  workit upgrade [--hosts=a,b|none] [--cli] [--preview | --yes | --apply --confirm | --check] [--set-updates=prompt|auto|off] [--json]
      Upgrade the CLI and every host after one confirmation, then verify with doctor; --check compares installed and latest versions
  workit launch <host> [--auto-upgrade] [-- <host args…>]
      Upgrade before host startup, then start the host
  workit doctor [--fix] [--fix-lock [--force [--yes]]]
      Verify the offline installation health (--fix installs the session trailer hook; --fix-lock clears a stale workit store lock)
  workit gc [--dry-run] [--prune-recovery --yes] [--worktrees [--apply]]
      Compact long task event logs, drop unreferenced blobs and old check logs; report (or prune) 2.x recovery copies; --worktrees lists (--apply removes) clean worktrees whose work is on the trunk
  workit dir <plans|retros|handoffs|config|state|data|cache|runtime>
      Print where a kind of file lives: plans, retros, handoffs per clone; config, state, data, cache, runtime per user
  workit completion <zsh|bash|fish|powershell>
      Print the shell completion script (setup and upgrade install it for $SHELL); verbs, subcommands, flags, check names, slice ids, workspaces
  workit uninstall
      Remove workit host registrations interactively (the Workit config dir is kept)
  workit grant [show|set|unset] [options]
      Show or change a workspace's autonomy grants (push, pr, merge, release, rerun) and default endpoint; raising needs the user at a terminal
  workit config show [options]
      Show the effective config here and where each value comes from
  workit workspace [list|add|set|rm] [options]
      Edit workspace entries without the wizard; a raise (rm included) needs the user at a terminal

Task control:
  workit <family> <action> [options]
      Inspect and control a Workit task; <family>: task, policy, evidence, finding, decision, worker, state

Delivery:
  workit check <name> [--full] [--task <id>] [--base <ref>] [--wait <dur> | --no-wait] [--no-lease --reason "<why>"] | workit check [--name <n>] [--shell] [--full] [--timeout <s>] [--task <id>] [--base <ref>] [--heavy [--wait <dur> | --no-wait]] [--no-lease --reason "<why>"] -- <cmd…>
      Run a configured or ad-hoc check and record CLI-observed evidence (exit = the command's); heavy checks wait for the machine-wide heavy-check lease
  workit lock status|reap|cancel|wait|run|heavy [options]
      The machine-wide heavy-check lease: who holds it, wait for it, run a command under it, and which shell commands count as heavy
  workit models show [options]
      The model and effort each role (decider, implementer tiers, verifier, reviewer, explore, babysit) runs on for a host, from models.roles, fanout.tierModels and the built-in defaults
  workit pr status|create|template|ready|edit|threads|reply|merge [options]
      PR/MR state with failing log tails and next action; open a SHA-verified PR; mark ready, edit, list and answer review threads; merge only when READY, verified and granted
  workit issue view|comment|close|create [options]
      Read, comment on, close or open a GitHub/GitLab issue on the workspace tracker (or --repo on the same host); writes need the pr grant and are recorded
  workit ci wait|rerun|logs [options]
      Wait for CI on the PR head (exit 0/1/3/4), read the failing jobs' log tails, or rerun failed jobs once per head
  workit git branch|commit|stage|unstage|push|rebase|hold|trailers [options]
      Policy-checked branch, hunk staging and commit (Workit-Session trailer); push with a lease and the tip verified
  workit release start|finish|publish|notes [options]
      git-flow releases without the git-flow binary: start a local release branch, finish it (merge, tag, merge back, push, forge release), publish it only when asked
  workit verify-delivery [push|pr|merge|release] [options]
      Observe that a push, PR head, merge or release really landed on the remote (exit 1 when not)
  workit stack plan|status|sync|restack|land [options]
      Plan, restack (lease push + retarget) and land a base-branch stack of PRs, root first
  workit fanout plan|brief|check|status|worktree [options]
      Register parallel slices (complete briefs, disjoint scopes, shared-file owners), render each worker's brief with the standing orders, watch them (STUCK, PR, CI, verdict, landed, landing order), make and release slice worktrees, and gate fan-in: out-of-scope edits, trunk and sibling merge conflicts
  workit ledger decision|ruling|verdict|list|check|verify-integrity|void|standing|add [options]
      Record and query decisions, rulings, SHA-keyed verdicts (patch-id carry across rebases) and a fanout's standing orders
  workit test-audit [paths…] [--diff [<base>]] [--rule <ids>] [--min-severity <level>] [--fail-on <level>] [--mutate [--test-cmd <cmd {files}>] [--max-mutants <n>] [--budget <s>] [--timeout <s>]]

content.content:
usage: workit git hold --why "<the user's words>" | --clear

Record the user's "not yet" for this branch: the Stop hook stops asking to push or open a PR until the next push or --clear (grants nothing)

A value that starts with - goes as --flag=value (or after a bare --).
usage: workit git commit -m|--message <msg>… | -F|--file <file|-> [--trailer <key: value>]… [--amend [--no-edit]] [--allow-empty] [-a|--all | --staged | [--whole] [--] <paths…>]

Commit (or --amend) with a linted Conventional Commit message, the session trailer (unless the workspace sets trailers: false) and any --trailer; a path staged in part commits its staged hunks only (--whole for all of it), --staged commits exactly the index

examples:
  workit git commit -m "fix(cli): answer help flags first" --all
  workit git commit -m "feat: x" --trailer "Co-Authored-By: Name <email>" --all
  workit git commit --amend --no-edit -- src/forgotten.ts
  workit git commit --staged -m "fix(a): one focused change"

A value that starts with - goes as --flag=value (or after a bare --).
